subject: Request: Makewhole bridge & term reset for AtlasWorks renewal
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Makewhole bridge & term reset for AtlasWorks renewal

Team —

Quick summary and ask: AtlasWorks (Strategic / FINTech) is at a renewal decision point; legal has delivered a competing platform ROI that is materially similar on token cost. They are asking for a one-time concession to bridge them to a new committed term.

Key facts:
- ARR at risk: $1.2M annual list
- Current renewal request: move entire workload to a 12-month committed plan but require a one-time "makewhole" credit to offset prior months + a term reset to align with their fiscal Q1.
- Customer ask: 22% one-time credit on the upcoming invoice (~$220k), term reset to 12 months, and a 99.95% SLA add-on for mission-critical workloads.
- They will commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (medium GPU pool) if we accept concessions.

Why this matters:
- AtlasWorks is a reference in payments fraud; retention opens cross-sell into their analytics and embedding contracts (TAM > $3M).
- Losing them risks competitor foothold in a vertical we're prioritizing this quarter.

Proposal (my recommended approval):
- One-time credit: 18% (compromise from their 22%)
- Term reset: 12 months starting Jan 1, 2027
- SLA add-on: trial 99.95% for first 6 months, auto-revert to standard SLA unless CS confirms steady ops
- Contingent: DocuSign amendment, 30-day payment milestone up front, and migration plan owned by CS.

Attachments: Atlas_renewal_MA_v3.pdf (proposed amendment), Atlas_usage_report_Q3.csv (usage profile)

Timeline: Customer expects a final yes/no by end-of-day Friday 12/4. Need exec OK for above variance vs standard playbooks.

Request: Vivek/Ben — can we get approval for the proposed package (18% credit + 12m term reset + SLA trial)? If not, what is absolute ceiling? I can brief Finance next.

Thanks —
Lukas
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Makewhole bridge & term reset for AtlasWorks renewal

Lukas —

Thanks for the concise brief. A few clarifying items before I can greenlight:
1) Margin impact: what is the net ARR delta after the credit amortized over the 12-month term? Please supply expected gross margin change and any expected usage uplift assumptions.
2) Precedent risk: do we have similar makewhole approvals in the last 12 months in this segment? If so, list them and outcomes.
3) SLA ask: 99.95% is a premium — what is the ops plan and runbook upgrade required from our side? Hannah, can CS承 confirm we can support that SLA for a 6-month trial without additional headcount?

If Finance signs off, I would be comfortable with an 18% credit cap but prefer a phased credit (10% upfront, 8% on milestone completion) to reduce churn risk.

Also: include a fallback option that keeps the price unchanged but adds a 6-month expanded PoC and training package — might be cheaper and buy us time.

Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations

Vivek / Lukas —

I endorse moving in the direction Lukas proposed, with one commercial tweak: offer 18% one-time credit but tie 6 percentage points (~6% equivalent) to milestones: (1) payment on signing, (2) migration completion to reserved capacity. That reduces exposure if they stall.

SLA: agree to a 6-month 99.9% SLA uplift (not full 99.95%) while CS runs an operational baseline. If CS validates after 6 months we can consider bumping to 99.95%.

This customer is strategic — losing them costs more than an 18% concession in near-term ARR. Hannah — can you confirm operational feasibility and training capacity? Attachment: Strategic_account_scorecard.xlsx (internal scorecard).

Ben
Head of Sales — Americas

From: Tom Rivera <tom@atlasworks.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Makewhole bridge & term reset for AtlasWorks renewal

Lukas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. After internal review we can accept the 18% one-time credit if Redwood will: (1) reset the term to 9 months instead of 12 (to align with our budget cadence), (2) commit to a 99.9% SLA for the first 6 months with a technical remediation credit if breached, and (3) provide two on-site (or virtual) training sessions for our engineers as part of onboarding.

We like the phased payment approach Ben suggested. If Redwood agrees to the above by 12/4 EOD, we will sign the amendment and move 70% of workload to the reserved capacity by Jan 1.

Tom Rivera
VP Product, AtlasWorks
